assessment.nobel_worthiness: A theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle, followed by experimental demonstration of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene, opened moire quantum matter as a tunable platform. This is the kind of new quantum behaviour in a material, anticipated by quantitative band theory and then confirmed, that I value most.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald supplied the continuum-model prediction and Jarillo-Herrero led the decisive experiments. The credited list does not name Yuan Cao, the first author of the key experiments, or other contributors, so a three-person prize leaves some credit questions.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have reproduced correlated states, superconductivity and related moire phenomena in the years since 2018, and theory explains much of the phenomenology. The origin of the superconductivity is still debated, but the core discovery is stable and timely.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of superconductivity in magic-angle graphene is unsettled.
The supplied credit omits some key experimental contributors, so the fairest configuration is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, with experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells and later in 3D materials, created a major branch of condensed matter physics and a new organising principle for electronic states. Its impact on materials discovery is large and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele gave the decisive theory, and Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental realisation in HgTe wells with Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang as predictors of that system. M. Zahid Hasan led the 3D observation, so the three-person limit forces a choice. Theory plus the first experiment is the cleanest configuration.
assessment.maturity: The field has had over fifteen years of independent confirmation by spectroscopy and transport, and the interpretation is robust. Recognition is somewhat overdue and has to be considered in light of the 2016 prize on topological phases.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions may weigh against it.
The credit for the HgTe prediction (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) and for 3D materials (Hasan and others) is not fully captured by the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, then giant values with crystalline MgO barriers, underpins magnetic read heads and MRAM. It is a clear measurable physical effect that is well understood in terms of spin-dependent tunnelling and band-structure symmetry filtering, which first-principles theory predicted quantitatively.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported room-temperature TMR in 1995, and Parkin and Yuasa et al. reached giant values with MgO in 2004. The three credited names cover the main experimental line. The theory of coherent tunnelling (Butler, Mathon) is not credited, and Yuasa is not among the names.
assessment.maturity: The effect has been confirmed in many laboratories and has been in commercial devices for years, so it is very mature. The GMR prize in 2007 covers adjacent ground, which may reduce the sense of novelty.
uncertainties: The MgO result involved other groups (Yuasa, Djayaprawira) not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory is a controlled non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons that explains the Mott transition and, combined with DFT, gives quantitative materials-specific predictions. Few theoretical methods have changed the study of real correlated materials so much, and it links directly to spectroscopy.
assessment.attribution: Georges and Kotliar developed the framework and mapped it to the Anderson impurity problem, and Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimension limit. Metzner is not in the supplied names, which leaves a genuine allocation problem in credit. I would propose Georges, Kotliar and Vollhardt as the supplied maximum.
assessment.maturity: The method is widely used and validated against experiments such as photoemission, and it is mature. Its prize case is a theoretical method, which makes it a less obvious discovery, but I think the case is strong.
uncertainties: Omission of Metzner from the credited names.
Whether the committee wants to recognise a computational method rather than a discovery of a phenomenon.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, reaches fractional uncertainty at the 10^-18 level and enables tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a redefinition of the second. It is a precision measurement achievement of high importance, though it lies partly outside my own area.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice and made the first demonstrations, and Ye's group pushed the accuracy and stability records. Two laureates is a natural and fair configuration, though other groups (Lemonde, Gill, Bloom) made significant contributions.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent laboratories confirm the performance at the highest level and the technology is changing metrology. The timing is good, as the redefinition of the second is under discussion.
uncertainties: I defer to colleagues in atomic physics on the relative merit versus ion clocks and the 2012 and 2005 prizes.
Credit for other optical clock groups is not covered by the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of high-temperature superconductivity in iron pnictides in 2008 was an unexpected result that created a second family of high-Tc materials and reopened the study of unconventional pairing. As a condensed-matter physicist I find the experimental surprise and the strong role of first-principles band structure attractive.
assessment.attribution: Kamihara and Hosono reported superconductivity in LaFeAsO(1-x)Fx and are the clear originators. Subsequent rapid advances in Tc by Chinese groups (e.g. Ren, Chen) are not in the credited names, so some people may feel excluded.
assessment.maturity: The materials are well confirmed and have been studied for over fifteen years. However, the pairing mechanism is not settled and Tc remains well below the cuprates, so the lasting impact is more limited than for the cuprates.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism is not established.
Credit for the follow-on Tc increases is outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Realising the Hubbard model with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, including the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, Fermi-Hubbard physics and single-site microscopy, gives a tunable quantum simulator for correlated matter. It is a major conceptual and experimental development with a direct link to condensed matter questions.
assessment.attribution: The theory proposal of Jaksch, Zoller and others and the experimental realisations by Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger are all part of the story. Cirac and Zoller are also credited, and a three-laureate cut is hard. I favour the experimental leaders, but this is an arbitrary choice at the margins.
assessment.maturity: The results are confirmed in many labs and the field is mature, but the benefit to solving open problems in solid-state physics is still modest. The 2001 BEC prize and the 2012 prize for single quantum systems overlap in the community.
uncertainties: Hard allocation among five credited names, including the theorists.
The extent to which simulation has actually resolved Hubbard-model questions is still unsettled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that magnetic order survives in monolayer and few-layer van der Waals crystals (CrI3, Cr2Ge2Te6) settled a question that the Mermin-Wagner theorem had suggested, through anisotropy, and opened a platform for gate-controlled magnetism. It is close to my own field of 2D magnets and spin dynamics.
assessment.attribution: The 2017 reports came from the groups of Xu (CrI3) and Zhang (Cr2Ge2Te6), and these two are the most defensible names. Jarillo-Herrero's related work on magnetic tunnelling and moire magnets is not the original discovery, and I would not name him. Other groups (Gong, Huang, Cheng) also contributed.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation is extensive and theory based on DFT and spin models explains the order, but the field is only nine years old. Recognition now would be early, and device impact is still developing.
uncertainties: Probably premature compared with more established discoveries.
Attribution is split among several 2017 papers and groups.
